newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour's Cullen calls for balanced policy mix.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour's Cullen calls for balanced policy mix.

text.p: Opposition Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen, commenting on December quarter inflation data, said on Friday that policy settings must be rebalanced to strengthen the export sector and reduce inflationary pressures.

"The latest figures show, yet again, that the present balance of monetary and economic policy is not able to deliver price stability without a seriously over-valued exchange rate," Cullen said in a statement.

Cullen said the data, which showed a 0.7 percent CPI rise for the December quarter versus economists' forecasts of 0.36 percent, meant further falls in interest rates were very unlikely in the near term.
"In its turn this will put further upward pressure on the exchange rate. Policies will have to change if the exchange rate is to drop while price stability is maintained."
He said "random hacking at government spending" by new Treasurer Winston Peters would not solve the problem.
